newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies close mixed, marks and Swiss higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies close mixed, marks and Swiss higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed, after key contracts recovered from support levels.
September Swiss francs and marks ended in positive territory after edging up from recent contract lows. Swiss made a fresh low early at $0.6584 and marks made their most recent contract low Monday.
September yen recovered from early lows as dollar resistance at 119 held back dollar/yen gains.
But some traders said the dollar bull trend remains intact and currency gains were only a minor correction in the overall downtrend.
"My tone is still bullish dollars and these are opportunities to sell (currencies)," a currency analyst said.
As for the extent of currencies' gains: "It's not too impressive and has not been some sort of big correction of any type," he said.
"It's been a little bit of a strange day," he added. "Look at the stock market, and they're actually selling dollars," he said. "I tend to think it's squaring ahead of all these numbers."
Currencies began firming before the release of June new home sales and continued to build gains after the report.
September yen futures saw fund buying and buy stops on their initial rally. Traders noted stops around $0.008500. Traders and technicians pegged support at $0.008388, $0.008400 and $0.008450.
June home sales rose 6.1 percent to a 819,000 annual unit rate from a downwardly revised 772,000 rate in May.
Many traders were said to be looking ahead to second-quarter gross domestic product and Friday's July jobs report.
Until then, one futures analyst said marks and Swiss may eke out more gains.

"Given the levels where we are, we've settled above critical support in marks at $0.5545 for two days in a row," the analyst said. He said a September Swiss move above $0.6680 would secure even more gains for the contract.
He said a more significant dollar pullback was needed to restore the health of the bullish dollar uptrend.

At the close, yen was off $0.000005 at $0.008493, marks rose $0.0002 to $0.5463, Swiss francs rose $0.0018 to $0.6641, sterling was flat at $1.6252, Canadian dollar rose $0.0024 to $0.7261, Aussie dollar lost $0.0016 to $0.7451, and Mexican peso rose $0.000025 to $0.126100.
